lesson_title: SA's Economy: Not What You Think It Is
hook_text: Everyone says South Africa runs on gold. The real number: mines and farms make less than R10 of every R100.
clip_script: Ask people what our economy is, and they say gold and mines. But out of every hundred rand the country produces, roughly sixty-five come from services, about twenty from factories and construction, and under ten from mines and farms together. We are a services economy with famous mines, not a mining economy with a few shops. One trap to dodge: small in rands does not mean unimportant. Farming makes only about three rand in every hundred, but it feeds the country and gives work in places where there are no other jobs.
visual_style: A stack of R100 notes splitting into three labelled piles — services, factories, mines and farms — with the tiny mining pile zoomed for shock effect.
pacing: Slow reveal of the guess, rapid-fire split of the real numbers, beat on the final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to map all three sectors and the infrastructure they ride on.
